newsitem.title: USA: Oakland, Calif., utility tax hike targets PG&E.
newsitem.headline: Oakland, Calif., utility tax hike targets PG&E.

text.p: The Oakland, Calif., City Council approved a special tax on Pacific Gas and Electric Co and other electric utilities that may operate in the city, city officials said Wednesday.

The council voted 5-3 in favor of the ordinance, creating a new business license tax category for electric utilities. City officials said revenues from the tax would raise about $1.2 million for the city's coffers.
Under the ordinance, PG&E and other utilities that may operate in the city would pay $6 per $1,000 of gross receipts.
The ordinance increases the utility business tax on PG&E sharply. PG&E has been paying about $1.20 per $1,000 in gross receipts.
PG&E said it would fight the new Oakland tax ordinance and possibly file a lawsuit to block it.
"We believe it's unconstitutional and illegal, and we plan to fight it," PG&E spokeswoman Jeanette Valentine said.
